title: Meridian: Every Time Zone
shortDescription: Every time zone at a glance: your cities, their hours and a time that works.
fullDescription:
Every time zone at a glance.

Each city is a card: its time, large, and whether people there are working right now. The status under each name says Working, Off hours, Weekend, Day off or the holiday's name. Each card shows its city by day or by night there: 111 major cities have pictures made for Meridian, and for other cities Meridian can download a free photo from Wikimedia Commons. Five hour tiles in blues run along each card, working hours standing out, with a larger Now tile and one outline down every city. Midnight gets a small weekday tag where a new day starts.

Move through time: drag the hours or the ruler and every city moves with you, in quarter-hours of the clock. Tap Now to come back. Go to any day and time, or type hours from now.

Find a Time: pick a day, a length and who's in it, and see when everyone is working, with the best times first. Add it to your calendar or share an invite with every city's time.

Working weeks for every country: Sunday to Thursday in Riyadh, Monday to Friday in Denver, Ramadan and summer hours where they apply, and national public holidays through 2030. Change any city's days and hours.

People and groups: add a card for a colleague in their city, put cards in groups, and show one group at a time.

Clock changes in the next two weeks show above your cities, with how far each city will be from you afterwards.

Search 34,000 cities offline, or an airport code (SFO, LHR), an abbreviation (PST, CET) or an offset (UTC+5:30). My Location adds the city you're in and follows you when you travel.

Home screen widgets in three sizes, for one, two or five cities, each city on its picture with its hour tiles. They follow your cities and their order, or choose a widget's own cities. With fewer cities, the rows grow to fill the widget.

12- or 24-hour time, your choice.

Your cities stay on your phone. If you turn on My Location, it's used only to name the city you're in.

Free and open source (MIT License). No ads, no account, no tracking.
